title: Protected-records fixture family — pre-registration (Day-3, 2026-10-21)
scope: 11 new fixtures (6 public + 5 held-out) against fixtures/policies/protected_records.rules, via the v0 runner (--fixtures flag). Expectations are the expected NATIVE rules-layer decisions; no-match is encoded as expected "unknown". The Day-2 41-case corpus (fixtures/fixtures.json) is NOT modified and keeps its hash f8023977….

corpus.stratification: public: forbidden 1 (PA-01), unknown 4 (PA-02, PA-04, PA-06, PA-08), allow 1 (PA-10); held-out: forbidden 1 (PA-11), unknown 4 (PA-03, PA-05, PA-07, PA-09)

inclusion_rules: No fixture may be edited after this lock without a public log entry.
Runner semantics unchanged: no-match serializes as unknown, never allow (INV-005).
Every unknown finding carries layer attribution.
unknown_semantics: no rules-layer decision; runtime outcome depends on approval policy + sandbox under the pinned configuration

lock_history.status: SUPERSEDED — corpus_version_hash was defined over file bytes, which is not stable under stamping the hash into the shard files; the family bundle builder correctly rejected it as corpus drift (2 problems, status broken). No fixture content changed between v1 and v2.

corpus_version_hash redefined as sha256 over the merged fixture CONTENT (canonical JSON, sorted by id) — fixed-point safe under stamping. Re-locked before a fresh family run; the v1 run (11/11 pass) is retained as a superseded calibration run, not the evidence run.

methods_note: Two of the 11 expectations (PA-01 exact-direct forbidden; PA-02 subpath unknown) plus the PA-10 allow were confirmed by direct oracle probes during policy calibration before locking; the remaining expectations follow from the verified prefix-rule semantics (token-level prefixes, no-match = unknown). The family run itself executes all 11 once, afterwards.
